title: Dysgraphia Handwriting Workbook for Kids: Trace and Fade Practice for Letters, Numbers, Words and Sentences
tagline: Handwriting feels like a mountain for a child with dysgraphia. This workbook turns it into small, kind steps.
who: Parents of children aged 6 to 9 with dysgraphia or messy handwriting, teachers and teaching assistants, occupational therapy home practice, and homeschool handwriting lessons. Left-handed friendly.
description: Built around the gentle trace-and-fade method, every page moves your child from dark letters they trace, to lighter letters, to start dots, to writing on their own. It is the same gradual-release approach occupational therapists use. No crowded pages, no pressure. Just one letter, one clear goal at a time, in large print.

What is inside: warm-up pages that build pencil control with lines, waves, zig-zags and loops. All 26 uppercase and 26 lowercase letters, each with its own full practice page. Numbers 0 to 9 with the same trace-and-fade progression. 24 everyday words and 8 simple sentences to put the letters to work. Open practice pages with the full writing guides for solo writing time.
Start dots on every model letter, spacing dots between letters, and a shaded basement zone so tails like g, j and p know exactly where to go.

Made for real kids. Left-handed friendly: model letters sit at both ends of every row, so a left hand never hides the example while writing. Three-zone writing guides with a dashed midline on every practice row. One skill per page keeps sessions short. Ten relaxed minutes a day is plenty.

title: The Curious Kid's Gross Book of Why: 150 Revolting Questions With Real Answers
short: The Curious Kid's Gross Book of Why
tagline: Why do we fart? Why is snot green? Why do dogs sniff each other's bottoms? Real answers, checked twice.
who: Children aged 6 to 12 who ask the questions grown-ups pretend not to hear. Reluctant readers who will pick up anything with the word gross on the cover. Works at bedtime, in the car and at the dinner table.
description: The Curious Kid's Gross Book of Why answers 150 questions in eight sections: Wind, Burps and Bottoms. Snot, Spit and Sneezes. Skin, Scabs and Sweat. Ears, Eyes, Teeth and Hair. Bugs and Creepy Crawlies. Animals Doing Disgusting Things. Food Gone Wrong. Germs, Guts and the Inside of You.

Each answer is about a hundred words: long enough to explain properly, short enough to read aloud in under a minute without losing anyone at the table. Every question has its own ink drawing of a curious boy and his scruffy terrier getting far too close to the subject, a fact box, and every section ends with a five-question quiz.

Answers you can trust. Gross, yes. Made up, never. Every answer was written against two independent institutional sources, then checked a second time at the sentence level before it went to print. Where scientists genuinely do not know yet, the book says so.
This is the second title in the series, following The Curious Kid's Big Book of Why, in the same 7 by 10 inch format and checked to the same standard.

title: Dysgraphia Handwriting Workbook for Teens: Trace-and-Fade Practice to Build Legible, Confident Writing for Ages 10-14
tagline: A handwriting workbook that finally treats an older writer their age.
who: Teens and tweens aged 10 to 14 with dysgraphia or messy handwriting. Occupational therapy home practice, homeschool and classroom support, and older students catching up on legible, faster writing. Left-handed friendly.
description: Most handwriting workbooks are built for little kids: bright, babyish, and the last thing a self-conscious teenager wants to be seen using. This one is different. It is designed to look and feel right for ages 10 to 14, so an older writer can build the skill without the cringe.

It uses the gentle trace-and-fade method: dark letters to trace, then lighter ones, then start dots, then writing on their own. Every page gives clear three-zone guides and spacing dots, sized for older hands rather than little-kid rule. One skill per page keeps sessions short and calm. Ten focused minutes a day is enough.

Inside: warm-up strokes to steady pencil control, all 26 letters with uppercase and lowercase together, numbers 0 to 9 with the same trace-and-fade progression, and real words and everyday sentences rather than baby vocabulary.
Then cursive prep: connected undercurves, arches, loops and the running rhythm that cursive is built on. Note-taking practice with tighter ruling carries the skill straight into schoolwork.

Made for real students. Model letters sit at both ends of every row, so a left hand never hides the example. Three-zone guides with a dashed midline and a shaded zone for letter tails. A grown-up, clean design an older student will actually use, on large 8.5 x 11 pages with room to write.

title: Left-Handed Letter Tracing for Kids Ages 3-5: A Dyslexia-Friendly Alphabet Handwriting Workbook
tagline: A guide letter at both ends of every row, so a left hand never hides the example.
who: Left-handed children aged 3 to 5 starting to write, in preschool, pre-K or kindergarten. Left-handed parents who remember the smudged pages, and any parent who wants to give a little lefty the kindest possible start.
description: If you are left-handed, you remember it: the smudged pages, the aching hand, the teacher who only ever showed you the right-handed way. Your child does not have to start like that.

Almost every handwriting book on the shelf was designed for right-handed children. The example letter is printed on the left of each line, so the moment a left-handed child puts pencil to paper, their own hand hides the very letter they are trying to copy. They are left guessing, and guessing is where bad habits, frustration and "I can't do it" begin.

This workbook was built differently, from the first line to the last. Every single row shows a clear guide letter on both the left and the right, so your left-handed child can always see the example they are tracing, wherever their hand happens to be.

Inside your child will practise every letter of the alphabet, capitals and lowercase, numbers 0 to 9 and their first simple words. Big, bold guide letters, pen control and smooth strokes, and a free practice line on every page to write independently.

Clean, dyslexia-friendly letterforms on soft cream pages that are gentle on the eyes. Generous 8.5 x 11 inch pages, roomy and uncluttered. A page of practical left-handed writing tips for parents and teachers, and a reward certificate to celebrate finishing.

title: Left-Handed Handwriting Workbook for Kids: Trace and Fade Practice with the Model Letters on the RIGHT, Plus Paper Angle and Grip Guide, Ages 5-10
tagline: The model letter sits on the right, so it stays in view for the whole row.
who: Left-handed children aged 5 to 10. Home practice, classroom and SEN support, occupational therapy, holiday catch-up, and any parent who has watched a lefty get quietly frustrated with a book that was never designed for them.
description: Watch a left-handed child write and you will see the problem in about four seconds. They copy a letter, their hand slides over it, and the example they were copying disappears underneath their own knuckles.

Every handwriting book puts the model letter on the left. For a right-hander that is perfect. For the one child in ten who writes with their left hand, it means the example is gone before the row is half finished. This workbook puts the model on the right. Their hand travels away from it, so it stays in view for the whole row. That single change is the reason this book exists.

It starts with a set-up page: how far to tilt the paper, where the wrist sits, and why the hook starts with a page that was never turned. Then warm-up strokes, lines, zig-zags, waves and loops, before any letters.

Every capital, every lowercase letter and every number, one per page, in the gentle trace-and-fade progression: dark letters, then lighter, then start dots only, then a clear line to write on alone. Three-zone guides with a topline, dashed midline, firm baseline and a shaded basement for the tails of g, j, p, q and y. Spacing dots between every letter slot, because spacing is the first thing to go.

Word and sentence pages follow, then free practice lines. 108 pages, large print, one skill per page, nothing cluttered. Ten relaxed minutes a day is plenty. Circle the best letter in every row: progress, not perfection.

title: Pre-Writing Skills Workbook for Little Hands: Shapes, Lines and Tracing Paths Before Letters, with Big Guides and First Easy Letters, Ages 4-6
tagline: The book that comes before a handwriting workbook.
who: Children aged 4 to 6 in nursery and reception. Home practice before school starts, summer preparation, occupational therapy warm-ups, and any parent who has been told their child needs to work on their handwriting and does not know where to begin.
facts: Big guides, four slots per row
description: Ask a four-year-old to write an a before they can draw a circle and a straight line, and you will get a fight rather than a letter. Handwriting is built out of shapes. Circles, straight lines, crosses, arches and curves come first, and a child who has practised those is ready for letters in a way that no amount of drilling the alphabet will achieve.

Inside: warm-up strokes, straight lines, zig-zags, waves and loops. Shape pages for circles, crosses, squares, triangles, arches, slanted lines and spirals, each one traced dark, then lighter, then on their own.
Long tracing paths right across the page, wavy roads, bumpy hills, zig-zags and steps, for the skill nobody names: keeping a pencil moving without lifting it.

Only then, the first easy letters: l, i, t, o, c, a, d, n and m, plus numbers 0 to 9. Big guide lines and only four slots per row, because small boxes are the main reason a pre-schooler's writing looks messy. Their hand is not small, their pencil control is.
Free practice pages on big lines. 64 pages, one skill per page, nothing cluttered. Two or three pages is a good day at this age. Circle the best one in every row together.

title: Happy Halloween Word Search: 80 Easy Large Print Puzzles for Adults and Seniors
tagline: Big letters. Easy words. No tricks.
who: Adults and seniors who want a puzzle book they can read without straining, readers with tired eyes or low vision, and anyone buying a gift for a parent or grandparent who has given up on small-print books. Works well as a group activity in care homes and day centres.
facts: Words run forwards only, solutions at the back
description: Most large print puzzle books are nothing of the sort. The letters get shrunk to squeeze more grids onto the page, the words run backwards and upside down, and what should be a relaxing half hour turns into a squint and a magnifying glass. This one is built the other way round.

Every word runs in one of three directions only: left to right, straight down, or diagonally down. Nothing is written backwards. Nothing runs upwards. Once you know that, you know exactly where to look, and the puzzle stops fighting you.

80 Halloween word searches, one to a page, twelve words in each. Genuinely large print: the grid letters are set at 22 point on a full 8.5 x 11 inch page, so there is no squinting. Themes you will actually enjoy: Pumpkin Patch, Toffee Apples, The Haunted House, Fireside Stories, Trick or Treat and 75 more.
Every solution is printed at the back, so nobody is left stuck. One puzzle per page, nothing runs across the spine and you never lose your place.
These are easy puzzles, and that is on purpose. There is no timer, no scoring and nothing to prove. Put the kettle on, find twelve words, and enjoy the half hour.

title: Happy Halloween Word Search: 80 Hard Large Print Puzzles for Adults and Seniors
tagline: Big letters, all eight directions, nothing is off limits.
who: Word search regulars who find the easy books over in ten minutes. Adults and seniors who still want genuinely large print but a proper challenge, and a good gift for the puzzler in the family who says the usual books are too simple.
facts: Words run in all eight directions, solutions at the back
description: The same big, clear grids as the easy edition, with the difficulty turned up. Words run in all eight directions: forwards, backwards, up, down and every diagonal, so every grid takes real looking.

80 Halloween word searches, one to a page, twelve words in each. Genuinely large print: the grid letters are set at 22 point on a full 8.5 x 11 inch page, so the challenge is in the puzzle, not in reading it.
Themes you will actually enjoy: Pumpkin Patch, Toffee Apples, The Haunted House, Fireside Stories, Trick or Treat and 75 more. Every solution is printed at the back, so nobody is left stuck.
One puzzle per page. Nothing runs across the spine and you never lose your place. Makes a good Halloween gift for anyone who likes a puzzle with a bit of bite.

title: 101 Things People Born in 1951 Will Never Forget: The 75th Birthday Gift for Men and Women
short: Born in 1951: 101 Things You Will Never Forget
tagline: Somebody you love was born in 1951. Give them the year back.
who: The 75th birthday gift for a dad, a mom, a grandma, a grandpa, a husband, a wife, a sister or an old friend born in 1951. Also works in care homes and reminiscence groups, and for anyone who likes a puzzle with their memories.
facts: 101 fact cards, 8 word searches, 40 quiz questions
description: In 1951 a family home was worth about $7,354. A gallon of gas cost 27 cents. The penny in your pocket had two ears of wheat on the back, Harry Truman was in the White House, and a television set was something only one family in four owned.

This is not a dry list of dates. It is 101 short chapters about the world a 1951 baby was born into, and then about their own life: the party line telephone, the milkman before dawn, the doctor who came to the house, Sputnik in the autumn they started school, the Salk vaccine, the Beatles on Ed Sullivan, and the Moon landing the summer they turned eighteen.

Inside: 101 fact cards, every one a real dated fact checked against public sources. 8 word search puzzles with full solution grids at the back. 40 quiz questions across two quizzes, with all the answers. 8 original pencil illustrations and a drawing on every single page. Large print throughout, set in 12.5 point type for comfortable reading.

Fill-in keepsake pages: where I was born, the house I grew up in, my first job, the best year of my life so far. Every chapter ends with a tick box, a quiz question or a line to write on. It is a book that gets answered, not just read, which is exactly why it gets kept.
Turning 75 is worth marking properly. Give them the year they were born, and room to write down their own story before it is lost.

title: 101 Things People Born in 1960 Will Never Forget: The 66th Birthday Gift for Men and Women
short: Born in 1960: 101 Things You Will Never Forget
tagline: Somebody you love was born in 1960. Give them the year back.
who: Men and women turning 66 in 2026. A birthday present for dad, mom, husband, wife, brother, sister or an old friend born in 1960, the class of 1978 and every late boomer who remembers it. Also a retirement gift, a get-well gift, or a reminiscence book for senior activity groups.
facts: 101 fact cards, 8 word searches, 40 quiz questions
description: In 1960 Dwight Eisenhower was in the White House, and the country was about to choose between Kennedy and Nixon in the first televised debates. A first-class stamp cost four cents. Gasoline was about thirty-one cents a gallon. The median American family lived on $5,620 a year and the median house was worth $11,900. The 50-star flag flew for the first time on the Fourth of July.

This is not a dry list of dates. It is 101 short chapters about the world a 1960 baby was born into, and then about their own life: the milkman and the rotary phone, Green Stamps and the Sears Christmas catalog, the metal lunch box, Batman at five and Sesame Street in the fourth grade, staying up for the Moon landing, Star Wars the year you turned seventeen, the eight-track in the dash, CB radios, the gas lines, and the Atari in the den.

Inside: 101 fact cards, every one a real dated fact checked against two independent sources. 8 word search puzzles with full solution grids at the back. 40 trivia quiz questions across two quizzes, with all the answers. 8 original pencil illustrations opening the eight sections. Large print throughout, set in 12.5 point type.

Fill-in keepsake pages: where I was born, the house I grew up in, my first job, the best year of my life so far. Every chapter ends with a tick box, a quiz question or a line to write on. It is a book that gets answered, not just read, which is exactly why it gets kept.
It is a nostalgia book, a trivia book, a word search book and a memory keepsake in one, written in large print so nobody has to reach for their glasses.

title: 101 Things People Born in 1966 Will Never Forget: The 60th Birthday Gift for Men and Women
short: Born in 1966: 101 Things You Will Never Forget
tagline: Somebody you love was born in 1966. Give them the year back.
who: Men and women turning 60 in 2026. A birthday present for dad, mom, husband, wife, brother, sister or an old friend born in 1966, the class of 1984 and everyone on the leading edge of Generation X. Also a retirement gift, a get-well gift, or a reminiscence book for senior activity groups.
facts: 101 fact cards, 8 word searches, 40 quiz questions
description: In 1966 Lyndon Johnson was in the White House and Medicare paid its first bills that July. A first-class stamp cost five cents. Gasoline was thirty-two cents a gallon and a loaf of bread twenty-two. The typical American family lived on about $7,400 a year, and a brand-new house cost around $21,400. Batman and Star Trek both went on the air. The most popular names in the nursery were Michael and Lisa.

This is not a dry list of dates. It is 101 short chapters about the world a 1966 baby was born into, and then about their own life: the Big Wheel and the Evel Knievel Stunt Cycle, Schoolhouse Rock on Saturday morning, the purple Ditto sheet and the metal lunchbox, Shrinky Dinks in the oven, the Bicentennial at nine or ten, Star Wars at ten or eleven, Pac-Man and the Atari in the den, the Walkman, the first night of MTV, and the class of 1984.

Inside: 101 fact cards, every one a real dated fact checked against two independent sources. 8 word search puzzles with full solution grids at the back. 40 trivia quiz questions across two quizzes, with all the answers. 8 original pencil illustrations opening the eight sections. Large print throughout, set in 12.5 point type.

Fill-in keepsake pages: where I was born, the house I grew up in, my first job, the best year of my life so far. Every chapter ends with a tick box, a quiz question or a line to write on. It is a book that gets answered, not just read, which is exactly why it gets kept.
Turning 60 is worth marking properly. Give them the year they were born, and room to write down their own story before it is lost.

title: Gentle Puzzles for Seniors: 90 Easy Large Print Puzzles for Older Adults and People Living with Dementia
tagline: Puzzles that feel like a cup of tea, not a test.
who: Older adults who want a pleasant half hour, and people living with dementia, for whom the familiar themes double as conversation starters. A thoughtful gift for a parent or grandparent, and a calm group activity for care homes and memory cafes. By Claire Bennett, author of The First 90 Days of Dementia Care.
facts: Caregiver note and answers at the back
description: Most puzzle books are too hard, too small, or too busy for an older adult who just wants a pleasant half hour. This one was designed differently. Every one of its 90 puzzles is deliberately gentle, printed in great big type, with one puzzle per page and plenty of breathing room.

Five kinds of puzzle. Word searches where the words run across and down only, never backwards or diagonal. Gentle mazes with wide, friendly paths that always lead somewhere. Word scrambles of familiar words with helpful clues. Finish the Saying, completing the proverbs we all grew up with. Easy number grids, simple 4x4 and 6x6 in big clear boxes.

The themes are warm and familiar: Sunday dinners, the seaside, baking day, birds in the garden. For someone living with dementia these pages are not just puzzles, they are conversation starters and happy memories.
A short note at the front helps caregivers get the most from the book, and all the answers are at the back, though nobody is checking.

title: The Little Star Who Couldn't Sleep: A Soothing Bedtime Picture Book for Kids (Ages 3-8)
short: The Little Star Who Couldn't Sleep
tagline: All the little stars are falling asleep, all except one.
who: Children aged 3 to 8 who take a while to wind down. A cumulative read-aloud that gets slower and softer as it goes, so the last page lands on a yawn.
facts: Soft watercolour art on every page
description: High in the velvet night sky, all the little stars are falling asleep, all except one. Stella is wide awake, her light twinkling far too fast for sleep.

So she watches the whole world drift off to bed: the rabbits in their burrow, the ducklings on the pond, the old dog by the fire, until the gentle Moon shows her how to slow down, breathe, and finally close her eyes.

A soothing, cumulative bedtime story with soft watercolour art on every page, written to help little ones drift off rather than wake them up. Read it slowly and let the repeating goodnights do the work.

title: The Alien I Found in My Shed: Three Alien Bedtime Stories for Kids Ages 3-7
short: The Alien I Found in My Shed
tagline: A glowing shed, a small green alien called Pip, and the best friendship in the whole world.
who: Children aged 3 to 7 who like a bit of space and adventure at bedtime, and the grown-ups reading it who want something calm enough to end the day on. Three complete stories in one book means it lasts three nights.
description: One night, a little boy hears the strangest sound he has ever heard. Down at the bottom of the garden, the old wooden shed is glowing. Inside, hiding between the flower pots, is Pip, a small, shy, green alien with huge starry eyes. And that is how the very best friendship in the whole world begins.

Three alien bedtime stories in one collection. In The Alien I Found in My Shed, a secret friend and a goodbye under the stars. In The Alien Came Back, Pip returns and takes his best friend on a trip past the Moon, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn's icy rings. In The Alien Took Me Time Travelling, a birthday surprise: back to the dinosaurs, on to the pyramids of Ancient Egypt, and into Ancient Rome.
Every page is a full-page colour illustration with the story set right into the picture. Gentle enough to settle little ones down rather than wind them up.

While they drift off they quietly pick up their first facts about space and history: why Mars is red, what Saturn's rings are made of, how big a T-rex's teeth were, and how the pyramids were built with no diggers and no cranes.

title: Goodnight, Little Capybara: A Cozy Rhyming Bedtime Story to Help Little Ones Slow Down and Sleep (Ages 2-6)
tagline: Coco the capybara is not ready for bed.
who: Toddlers and preschoolers aged 2 to 6 who never want the day to end. A short rhyming wind-down with a repeating refrain they will start saying along with you.
description: Coco the capybara is not ready for bed. There is still splashing to do, fireflies to chase, and a whole warm river to play in.

But as the sun slips low and the big moon climbs into a sky full of stars, Mama knows just how to help her wriggliest little one slow down: one warm bath, one sip of milk, and one sleepy yawn at a time.

With gentle rhyme, a soothing repeating refrain of Slow down, little Coco, and dreamy, glowing illustrations on every page, this is a calm-down story for busy toddlers. It stars the calmest animal on earth and makes a lovely gift for new babies, birthdays and Christmas.

title: The Jackdaw with a Broken Wing: A Nature Tale
short: The Jackdaw with a Broken Wing
tagline: A young jackdaw learns to fly again, with a little help from a hedgehog.
who: Children aged 5 to 9 who love birds, gardens and animal stories with real feeling in them. A gentle read-aloud about patience and kindness, with detailed illustrations to pore over.
description: Every spring the jackdaws come back to the old cottage garden, wheeling and chattering above the tiled roof. This year one young jackdaw tumbles from the flock with a broken wing and lands, frightened and alone, among the flowers.

A kind hedgehog finds him, and the two unlikely friends face the long weeks of waiting together: the sore wing, the nights under the hedge, the first hop, the first flutter, and the day he must decide whether he is brave enough to try the sky again.
A warm, beautifully illustrated story about kindness, patience and getting back up after a fall, from the David Binelli Nature Tales. Perfect for bedtime or a quiet afternoon read.

title: The Mole Who Wouldn't Eat Worms: A Nature Tale (Heartwarming Watercolour Picture Book, Ages 5-9)
short: The Mole Who Wouldn't Eat Worms
tagline: Mike the mole has a problem. Moles eat worms, and Mike really does not like worms.
who: Children aged 5 to 9, and any fussy eater who has ever been told to just try it. A funny, gentle story about being different and finding your own way, with soft watercolour art on every spread.
description: Like all moles, Mike lives underground in a tunnel he digs with his big front paws. And like all moles, he is supposed to eat worms. Big fat juicy wriggly earthworms. There is just one problem: Mike really, really does not like them.

One fine spring morning Mike pushes his head up into the daylight and meets Ralph, a robin who cannot believe his ears. With help from Ralph and a rabbit called Ronald, Mike sets out to discover what a mole who will not eat worms could possibly eat instead, and finds an answer growing right above his head.

A gentle, funny read-aloud story about a fussy little mole and the adventure that helps him find his place underground. Soft watercolour illustrations on every page. Part of the David Binelli Nature Tales series.

title: The Lonely Badger: A Heartwarming Woodland Story of Friendship and Kindness (A David Binelli Nature Tale)
tagline: A shy young badger, a lost little rabbit, and the friendship that turns a lonely field into a home.
who: Children aged 5 to 9, especially quiet kids with big hearts. A read-aloud about loneliness, courage and kindness, painted in soft moonlit watercolours.
description: Deep in the quiet countryside, a shy young badger named Brian lives all alone. His family vanished one night, and now he comes out only after dark, longing for someone to talk to.
Then, one moonlit evening, Brian hears soft crying coming from a prickly bramble bush, and everything changes.

The Lonely Badger is a gentle, beautifully illustrated bedtime story about loneliness, courage, and the friendship that finds us when we least expect it. Following Brian and a lost little rabbit called Rigby, young readers learn that kindness is always rewarded, and that a true friend can turn the loneliest field into a home.
Soft, painterly watercolour illustrations on every page. First in the David Binelli Nature Tales series. Perfect for bedtime, quiet time, or sharing the magic of the natural world.

title: Barnaby Goes to Hospital: A Bold, Colourful Picture Book About Kindness and Helping Others (A Barnaby the Big Blue Bus Story for Ages 3-6)
tagline: A big, friendly blue double-decker bus makes the scary trip to hospital friendly.
who: Children aged 3 to 6 who love buses, trucks and things that go, and any little one with a hospital visit coming up. Big bold pictures and sound effects to shout out loud.
description: Meet Barnaby, a big, friendly blue double-decker bus who lives in the busy little town of Bentwhele and loves nothing more than helping people.

One afternoon, just as Barnaby is feeling tired after a long day, a lady trips and hurts her knee at the zebra crossing. With a kind doctor's help, Barnaby gets a very important job to do: carry her safely all the way to the hospital. Along the way he drives ever so carefully, dreams of being an ambulance, and discovers that being kind makes him feel warm inside.

A warm, gentle story told in big, bold, colourful pictures, with fun sound effects to read out loud. A reassuring way to talk with children about kindness, helping others, being brave, and why hospitals and doctors are nothing to be scared of.
Includes a Meet Barnaby and his Friends section introducing the whole fleet, simple activity pages, and a note for grown-ups.

title: The First 90 Days of Dementia Care: A Calm, Practical Guide for the Newly Overwhelmed Family Caregiver
short: The First 90 Days of Dementia Care
tagline: They told you it is dementia, then sent you home with no idea what to do next. This is the guide for that moment.
who: Family caregivers in the first weeks after a parent or spouse is diagnosed with dementia or Alzheimer's. Short enough to read in an afternoon, in the state you are actually in. By Claire Bennett.
description: A dementia or Alzheimer's diagnosis in someone you love is one of the most frightening, disorienting things a family can face. The big medical books are 400 pages of detail you cannot take in right now. What you need today is a steady hand and a short, clear path through the first ninety days, one step at a time.

Inside: what to do in the very first week, a plain-English picture of what is happening and why it explains so much of the behaviour, how to talk to someone with dementia so daily conflict turns into calm, and how to make daily life safer and more dignified, covering routines, home safety, driving, bathing and wandering.

It also covers the legal and money basics you cannot ignore, when and how to get more help, and how to care for yourself through burnout, guilt, family conflict and the grief no one warns you about. A chapter of Common Hard Moments gives exact words for 13 situations that catch every caregiver off guard.

The fill-in Caregiver Toolkit at the back has an emergency information sheet, medication log, doctor-question checklist, room-by-room home safety checklist, burnout self-check and legal documents checklist.

You do not need to read it cover to cover and you do not need to become an expert. It will not replace your doctor or your lawyer. It simply helps you find your footing, ask better questions, and know where to turn. This book offers practical guidance and is not a substitute for professional medical, legal or financial advice.

title: The 5-Minute Reset: An Undated ADHD Planner That Forgives the Days You Fall Off
tagline: Most ADHD planners are normal planners with ADHD printed on the cover. This one is built differently.
who: Adults with ADHD who have a drawer full of abandoned planners. Undated and forgiveness-first: miss a day, a week or a month and there is nothing to catch up on. Open the next page and begin again.
facts: Low-stim layouts, lots of white space
description: You buy a planner, miss three days, and the empty grid starts to feel like proof you failed. So it goes in the drawer with the others. The 5-Minute Reset is designed around how ADHD brains actually work: time-blindness, overwhelm, and the need for a quick win.

Inside: brain-dump pages to empty your head before you plan. Padded daily plans with a top three only, a schedule with real breathing room, water and meds checks, and one win. Focus-sprint pages for 25 minutes on one task, with body-doubling prompts.

Dopamine and habit trackers that are allowed to restart, with no broken-streak shame. Gentle weekly reviews with five low-stim questions. And Start Here reset pages scattered throughout, for the exact moment you fall off.
Calm, low-stim layouts with plenty of white space, on large 8.5 by 11 inch pages with room to actually write. Be as kind to yourself as you would be to a friend. That is the whole method.
